LLM auditresponse for notemark.js:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The file is a Node.js/Electron launcher script (`notemark.js`) that resolves the application directory from command-line arguments (`--app`), environment variables (`_APPDIR`), or default system paths (`/usr/lib/@appname@`). It adjusts `process.resourcesPath`, sets production environment flags for packaged apps, and optionally wraps `fs` methods to redirect filesystem lookups from Electron's default resources path to the resolved app directory.

There are no network requests, no downloads, no `eval`/`base64` obfuscation, no credential exfiltration, and no modification of unrelated system files. The `@appname@` placeholder indicates standard PKGBUILD templating. All behavior is consistent with an Electron application wrapper relocating its resources for system-wide installation on Arch Linux, which is normal upstream application functionality, not a supply-chain attack.
</details>
<evidence>

<summary>
Electron app path resolver; no network, exfiltration, or obfuscation detected.
</summary>
</security_assessment>

There is no evidence of obfuscation, data exfiltration, reverse shells, credential theft, or execution of code from untrusted hosts. LLM auditresponse for notemark.sh:


<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The file is a standard Electron application wrapper script for the notemark package. It sets up environment variables (LD_LIBRARY_PATH, CHROME_DESKTOP), determines the application bundle location (app.asar, app, or app.asar.unpacked), conditionally disables the Chrome sandbox when running as root (a standard Electron practice), and selects an appropriate Ozone platform (X11/Wayland). The final exec launches the system-installed Electron binary with the application's entry point. All behavior is consistent with legitimate Electron app packaging on Arch Linux. No suspicious network activity, obfuscation, file exfiltration, or arbitrary code execution was found.
</details>
